idiom_name: tower::Service + Layer middleware chain (or a hand-rolled Box<dyn Service> chain)
implementation_notes: The ecosystem supplies the chain: tower::Service is the request-in/response-out abstraction and a Layer wraps one service in another, so a gate is a layer that verifies the request and either returns an error or delegates to the inner service's call; async HTTP stacks built on tower make the gate chain configuration rather than code and propagate backpressure through poll_ready. What replaces the classic structure: trait objects (Box<dyn Service<..>>) and Layer composition replace proxy classes and a hand-built chain, and the borrow checker forces each gate to own or mutably borrow its inner service explicitly; the verified identity travels in typed request extensions rather than in a stringly header. In a crate that cannot depend on tower, the same shape is hand-rolled as a Box<dyn Service> chain - more code, and getting poll_ready backpressure right becomes your job.
pitfalls: A Service may panic if call is invoked without a successful poll_ready, and cloning an inner service for a boxed future can yield an unready clone; take the ready service with std::mem::replace.
Identity placed in request extensions can be inserted by any code holding the request, so the extension type must be private to the crate or it can be forged.
A gate that introduces its own error type stops the type-level composition of the chain and forces boxing or a shared error enum on every layer.
